Data-center revenue grew 3% and then 2% sequentially in the two quarters ending August and November 2025, the steepest part of the hyperscaler capex ramp, and the cause was inside custom both times: management guided data center flat sequentially in Q3 FY2026 "with electro-optics strength offset by lower custom revenue" and then reported "a sequential decline in our custom revenue due to lumpiness in demand." Merchant optics supplied the growth in both quarters.

Technology shifts that change the slope. Co-packaged optics moves the optics onto the switch or accelerator package and removes the pluggable DSP socket where Marvell's largest revenue line is booked.▪ Marvell's stated position is that "pluggable modules remain the primary form factor for scale-out networks, and we do not expect that to change" (Q2 FY2027 call), which is an assumption under the largest revenue line in the company; Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 "Davisson" is a 102.4T co-packaged part (nextplatform.com, accessed 2026-08-28) [web]. Linear pluggable optics attacks the same socket by deleting the DSP and driving optics from the switch SerDes, but adoption has lagged the early forecasts, with the IEEE overview describing it as limited at 800G against entrenched DSP infrastructure. Scale-up links are copper today, which routes the dollar to AEC DSPs and cables, and Credo took that volume. Scale-up protocol standards are unsettled across UALink, Ethernet-for-Scale-Up-Networking and NVLink Fusion. Memory scarcity is a real and new content gain pulling demand into CXL memory expansion, and it is a scarcity-driven substitution that reverses when memory supply normalizes.

Policy. BIS rules of October 2022, October 2023, November 2024 and January 2025 progressively expanded licensing requirements on advanced computing integrated circuits to China; the AI Diffusion Rule issued in January 2025 was to be cancelled and replaced, which the 10-K describes as creating uncertainty. China by destination was 43% of revenue in FY2024 and FY2025 and 36% in FY2026, and the 10-K states a substantial majority of China shipments are for non-China customers manufacturing inside China. Taiwan went from 3% of revenue in FY2024 to 20% in FY2026, which tracks AI system assembly. The FY2026 risk factors newly disclose a 2025 precedent in which US government interactions implied a 15% remittance of gross China-derived revenue as a condition of export licences, which "did not impact Marvell" and, if applied, "could erode our gross margins, reduce our pricing flexibility, and potentially prompt us to curtail or discontinue sales in China."

What would show first if the trend were breaking, ordered by how early each disclosed item moves:

  • Custom revenue linearity within FY2027, since management guides a second-half ramp and the same pattern in FY2026 produced a Q3 sequential decline.
  • Non-GAAP gross margin against the 57.5–58.5% Q3 guide, where a faster decline says custom is a larger share of the incremental dollar than disclosed and a flat margin says custom is not ramping.
  • Interconnect growth against the 65% transceiver-market forecast.
  • Capacity prepayments rising while sequential data-center growth decelerates.
  • A step-down in the Distributor A or Direct Customer A percentages without an offsetting new name.
  • Taiwan destination revenue, the closest proxy in the filings for AI system assembly volume.
  • The count of vested Google warrant tranches, each of which marks $500m of cumulative custom revenue from that customer.

7. Critical points

1. Ten years of revenue produced $27m of cumulative GAAP operating income, and two asset sales produced all the cumulative profit. Across FY2017 to FY2026 Marvell generated $43,096m of revenue and $26.8m of cumulative GAAP operating income, with operating losses in five of the ten years. Cumulative GAAP net income of $1,937m over the same decade is less than the sum of two disposal gains: $1,123m of other income plus a $786m tax benefit on the Wi-Fi sale to NXP in FY2020, and $1,830m pre-tax on the automotive Ethernet sale to Infineon in FY2026. The drag is amortization of acquired intangibles, $6,169m across the decade and $942m in FY2026 alone, arising from roughly $22bn of acquisitions. That is not an artifact to exclude when testing durability: the IP platform Marvell says wins custom sockets was bought, and the purchase price has consumed the entire ten-year operating profit stream.

2. The growth is real and the margin is going the other way, and the two are the same event. Revenue grew 42% in FY2026 and is guided to about 45% in FY2027 and 50% in FY2028, while non-GAAP gross margin has declined in each of the last four fiscal years to 58.9% in each of the first two quarters of FY2027. The CFO named the driver: "Part of the acceleration story in Q3, as you point out, mix is the primary driver. We've got a strong ramp in custom." Custom silicon converts revenue to gross profit at an estimated 30–44% against 63–66% for merchant, so each point of mix moved from merchant to custom costs roughly a quarter-point of consolidated gross margin, and management's own FY2029 custom target moves that mix by about twenty points.▪ Section 8 sets the margin series against the claim that custom is the highest-quality growth.

3. Operating margin expansion has come from cost restraint, not from the product. FY2026 non-GAAP operating margin of 35.3% is statistically the same as FY2023's 35.5%, on revenue 38% higher. Inside that, non-GAAP gross margin gave up 5.0 points and non-GAAP operating expense declined 4.8 points of revenue.▪ Headcount went from 7,448 at FY2023 year end to 7,480 at FY2026 while revenue per employee went from $795k to $1,096k, and FY2026 R&D dollars grew 6.4% against 42% revenue growth, putting R&D at 25.3% of revenue, the lowest ratio in the ten-year series. That ratio has already turned back up: 27.0% in Q1 FY2027 and 27.1% in Q2, with R&D dollars up 43% year over year against 37% revenue growth.

4. The custom franchise's one durability test to date went against it. Marvell designed Amazon's Trainium 2, the programme that took custom revenue from roughly zero to $1.5bn. Independent reporting places Trainium 3 with Alchip on the back end and Annapurna on the front end, attributing the loss to Trainium 2 execution [web], and Benchmark downgraded the stock on 2025-12-08 on that basis, with the shares declining 9% intraday. Alchip's revenue then rose 82.6% sequentially in the June 2026 quarter as N3 accelerator production began. Marvell's own slide puts XPU socket life at 18 to 24 months, so the FY2029 target of above $10bn implies holding roughly three consecutive rebids at every programme between 2025 and 2028, on a base where the flagship programme's next generations already moved.

5. Concentration has risen in every year of the disclosed series and the counterparties are unnamed. Distributor A was 12% of revenue in FY2020 and 45% in Q1 FY2027, and three customers were 75% of gross accounts receivable at 2026-05-02 against five at 72% a year earlier. Because that distributor resells to multiple end customers, the true end-customer concentration is higher than any single disclosed number and cannot be derived from the filings, so neither the identity nor the depth of the largest reported relationship in the company is observable. Section 8 sets the full series against the claim that design-win breadth is diversification.

6. Cash has stopped following revenue. FY2026 free cash flow of $1,396m was unchanged from FY2025's $1,397m on $2,427m more revenue, and the free-cash-flow margin declined from 24.2% to 17.0%. Three things absorb the gap. Working capital consumed roughly $1.1bn as receivables more than doubled and days sales outstanding went from 65 to 97. Technology-licence obligations, paid quarterly and classified as financing, have taken $128m–$154m a year since FY2022 and fall below free cash flow as normally computed, so FY2026's $1,396m becomes $1,268m once they are deducted. And roughly $1bn of supplier capacity prepayments is planned for FY2027, a cash outflow with no precedent at this scale in the prior decade, of which $333.7m had already landed in the first half.

7. Equity has become the currency for customers and technology. Within five months Marvell issued $2.0bn of convertible preferred to NVIDIA convertible into up to 21,778,000 shares, issued 24.5m shares plus up to 22.4m contingent shares and roughly $233m of contingent cash for Celestial AI, and issued Google a warrant over up to 58,970,907 shares. Against a base of roughly 876m shares outstanding at 2026-08-01, the disclosed potential dilution stack is 124.6m shares, or 14.2%.▪ The FY2026 buyback of 26.6m shares for $2,040m was offset ten days into FY2027 by 26.6m shares issued for Celestial AI and XConn at almost the same price (§10.1). Stock-based compensation more than doubled year over year in Q2 FY2027 to $326.2m, 11.9% of revenue, and cash paid to withhold shares on vesting rose 3.6x to $365.2m in the half.

8. Interconnect supplies roughly nine-tenths of the FY2027 data-center increase, and it is the model's largest lever. Data center is guided to grow about 60% in FY2027 with interconnect above 70% and custom's written guide at "more than 20%", so roughly 88% to 92% of the FY2027 data-center dollar increase comes from merchant lines▪ [estimate: management's disclosed growth guides applied to disclosed FY2026 revenue]. Murphy attributed "probably the most meaningful part" of the $1.5bn FY2028 revenue raise to scale-up optics and switching. In the forward model, an eight-point annual move in interconnect growth swings FY2033 non-GAAP operating income by $8.2bn against $4.5bn for a ten-point move in custom growth (§17).

9. Management's forward number has moved five consecutive times in one direction, on the same stated evidence base. The FY2027 revenue outlook went from approximately $9.5bn in September 2025 to $10bn, $11bn, $11.5bn and $12bn across five communications in eleven months; FY2028 went from approximately $13bn to $18bn in nine months. FY2027 data-center growth was forecast at approximately 25% in December 2025 and approximately 60% in August 2026, a 35-point revision to the same fiscal year. December's call had described that forecast as based on "robust demand signals and strong bookings across our entire portfolio." The same extrapolation ran the other way in the last downcycle: in May 2023 management expected second-half acceleration "accompanied by gross and operating margin expansion" and FY2024 revenue declined 7.0%.

10. Two of the three biggest unknowns are dated. The custom gross margin, which is the largest swing factor in any FY2029 answer, has never been disclosed and cannot be derived from a single-segment filing. The Google warrant's grant-date fair value, which sets the contra-revenue rate, will first appear in the Q3 FY2027 10-Q. And management has said the long-term operating model will be reset at an Investor Day on 2026-10-06, five weeks after the run date, where the dormant 64–66% gross-margin target, the FY2029 custom figure and the CY2028 market estimate are all candidates to move.

8. Management claim pressure tests

The Google warrant is presented as validation. The 8-K describes discretionary purchases and prices the relationship. The framing after 2026-08-19 was of a $120bn agreement and a sweep of all four US hyperscalers. The instrument contains no purchase obligation: 57,610,040 of 58,970,907 warrant shares, 97.7%, vest only on "discretionary purchases … by or on behalf of Google and its affiliates," and the remaining 1,360,867 vest on time. Management said on the Q2 FY2027 call that revenue from the covered programmes through FY2028 already sat inside the existing custom guide, so the agreement adds nothing to the guided period. What is new is the payment: an estimated $6bn to $10bn of grant-date fair value, roughly 5% to 8% of the revenue it vests against, recorded as a reduction of revenue as that revenue is recognized. On a 35% pre-warrant custom gross margin that takes the reported margin on Google programmes to about 29%-31%. Full vesting requires $18.5bn a year of Google custom revenue for six and a half years against total company revenue of $8.2bn in FY2026.

Custom is described as the highest-quality growth. It is the lowest-margin revenue in the company and its share of the company declines in FY2027. Custom was 18.3% of FY2026 revenue and works out to 15%–21% of the ~$12bn FY2027 guide depending on where "more than 20%" lands. Within data center it goes from about 25% of FY2026 revenue toward 19% at the written guide, or holds near 25% only if it grows about 60%. Marvell's non-GAAP gross margin has declined in every year since custom production began, 6.5 points from FY2023 to the Q3 FY2027 guide, roughly $780m of gross profit at the ~$12,000m FY2027 revenue run rate, and management named the custom ramp as the cause of the current step. The CEO put the scale question himself in March 2026: "if you look at this year and you look at us driving the company to $11 billion, and then you unpack things like custom, it's not that big a percentage of the total."

Multi-generational engagement is offered as the durability mechanism. The socket life is 18 to 24 months and it is Marvell's own figure. [deck: 2025-06-17, slide 23]. The FY2029 target of above $10bn implies holding 20% share of a $55.4bn CY2028 market, which requires winning roughly three consecutive rebids at every programme between 2025 and 2028, on a base where the flagship programme's next generations already went elsewhere.

Design-win breadth is offered as diversification. Concentration rose every year. Eighteen sockets at June 2025 and above twenty by March 2026, against Distributor A at 24% of FY2024 revenue and 45% of Q1 FY2027, Direct Customer A from under 10% to 16%, and three customers at 75% of gross receivables. Marvell's own peer comparison runs the other way: Credo's largest customer declined from 67% to 49% of revenue over the same window while Marvell's largest relationship grew.

The FY2029 custom target and the CY2028 share target cannot both hold with a normal merchant year. Twenty percent of the $94bn CY2028 data-center market is $18.8bn of FY2029 data-center revenue, and management confirmed the mapping on the Q1 FY2027 call. Subtracting the $10bn-plus custom target leaves $8.8bn for interconnect, switching and storage in FY2029, against $11.1bn–$11.6bn implied for FY2028 by management's own guides.▪ That is a decline of 21% to 24% in the merchant franchises during a year management describes as accelerating [estimate: 20% of the disclosed CY2028 market less the disclosed FY2029 custom target, against FY2028 derived from management's own growth guides]. The two targets were set fourteen months apart on different market estimates and have not been reconciled.

The FY2027 communications target and the FY2027 quarterly guidance are inconsistent. On the same call management said it expects FY2027 communications growth "to approach our 10% target" and guided Q3 down 13%–15% both sequentially and year over year with a "solid sequential recovery" in Q4. First-half actual was $1,152.9m and the Q3 midpoint is about $487m, so a 10% full-year outcome needs a Q4 of roughly $660m, a 36% sequential increase against a nine-quarter maximum of 13.8%. The quarterly path implies +2.7% to +6.4% for the year. The wording had already moved from "approximately 10%" on the two prior calls.

The FY2026 gross-margin improvement is presented as mix. Most of it is a prior-year charge unwinding. GAAP gross margin went from 41.3% to 51.0%, 9.7 points. Restructuring inside cost of goods sold contributed 6.2 points by not repeating, acquired-intangible amortization inside cost of goods sold another 4.7 points by declining from $721.7m to $639.0m, lower stock compensation 0.2 points, and the underlying product margin subtracted 1.5 points. Adding back the $357.9m of FY2025 restructuring in cost of goods sold gives a like-for-like improvement of 3.5 points.

The stated capital-return policy was missed in four consecutive years and has quietly dropped out of the language. The 2021 investor day set "Returns to shareholders (>50% of FCF)" as the third ranked priority [deck: 2021-10-06, slide 123], a figure that also appears on the Inphi M&A call, at the 2020 investor day and on the Q1 FY2023 call. Payouts were 27%, 30%, 30% and 35% of free cash flow in FY2021 through FY2024, and the gap was explained at the time by the need to pay down Inphi debt first. Two years funded from asset sales produce the ten-year average of 84%: 191% in FY2020 after the NXP proceeds and 161% in FY2026 after the Infineon proceeds. The current formulation drops the percentage: "we intend to continue repurchasing shares to manage dilution" (Q2 FY2027 call).

Peer comparison at the margin line does not support the leadership framing on like products. Management describes "market-leading franchises in optical DSPs, switching and broadband analog components" (Q2 FY2027 call). The estimated merchant gross margin of 63–66% is roughly four to seven points below Broadcom's semiconductor-segment gross margin of approximately 70% in the quarter ended 2026-05-03, and Broadcom's rose over the same period while Marvell's declined. On switching specifically an analyst put Marvell's share as "relatively small" on the Q1 FY2027 call and the premise was not corrected. On the six-to-seven point gap applied to an FY2026 interconnect base of $2,880m bottom-up or $3,050m on management’s “roughly half” of data center, the difference is $170m–$210m of annual gross profit [estimate: the estimated merchant-margin gap applied to the estimated interconnect base].

The market estimate behind the share target was raised 25% in fourteen months on an unchanged base. The CY2028 data-center market went from $75bn (April 2024) to $94bn (June 2025) with the CY2023 base of $21bn unchanged and the same source list, moving the compound rate from 29% to 35%; compute was restated up 29% and interconnect 37%.▪ Inside the April 2024 deck, two consecutive slides show custom's CY2028 figure moving from $27.5bn to $42.9bn purely by raising custom's assumed share of accelerated compute from 16% to 25%. The share target is stated as a percentage, so a further revision changes the implied revenue without changing the headline. Against that denominator Marvell is gaining share; against Broadcom's disclosed AI revenue its position in the two-company pool declined from 37% in CY2023 to about 15% on CY2026 guidance.

Five inflections.

  • April 2016: a forced management change ends the consumer company. Revenue declined from $3,637m in FY2015 to $2,301m in FY2017, a 37% contraction, and FY2016 produced a $745m operating loss of which $736m was the Carnegie Mellon litigation settlement. By FY2018 the rebuilt company produced $2,409m of revenue at a 60.7% gross margin and a 17.8% GAAP operating margin, still the highest GAAP operating margin Marvell has reported. The precedent it set is that Marvell will abandon a whole end market: mobile went in 2015, Wi-Fi in 2019, automotive Ethernet in 2025.
  • July 2018 to April 2021: buying a new company with debt and stock. Goodwill went from $1,993m to $11,511m, acquired intangibles from nil to a $6,153m peak, long-term debt from nil to $4,485m, and basic weighted-average shares from 498m to 797m. That is a 61% increase in four years against an 85% revenue increase, so revenue per share improved 16%. The cost appears in GAAP earnings: roughly $5.2bn of purchase-price amortization across five years, and GAAP operating losses in FY2020, FY2021, FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025.
  • FY2024 to FY2025: the non-AI half collapses and R&D is redirected. The four non-data-center end markets went from $3,511m to $1,603m in two years. In Q3 FY2025 the board approved a plan that cancelled future product releases in those markets and moved the spending to data center, at a cost of $711.8m. Data center's share of revenue moved from 41% to 72% in two years, and the denominator shrank as much as the numerator grew. The behaviour is now embedded in the reporting: in Q4 FY2026 the four markets were consolidated into one line and are no longer separately observable.
  • FY2026 to FY2027: revenue accelerates while the promised margin does not arrive. Management raised the forward outlook five consecutive times, and the FY2028 figure rose $5bn in nine months. FY2026 non-GAAP operating margin of 35.3% is the same as FY2023's on 38% more revenue, with gross margin down 5.0 points and operating expense down 4.8 points of revenue. Free cash flow was flat on $2,427m more revenue.
  • 2026: equity becomes the currency for customers and technology. The NVIDIA preferred, the Celestial shares and earnout, and the Google warrant together put roughly 125m potential shares against a base of about 876m, and the customer warrants are recorded as a reduction of revenue, so the top line absorbs the cost while the dilution runs separately. The Celestial earnout is remeasured against Marvell's own share price each quarter, producing a $331.8m charge in Q1 FY2027 alone; a cash-settled forward stock purchase contract with a $300.0m notional and a twelve-month term was entered in April 2026 to offset part of that exposure, against an earnout running to FY2029.

How this company behaves. Under a downturn it defunds, then divests, then stops reporting the line — mobile, Wi-Fi, the FY2025 R&D redirection, automotive Ethernet, then the Q4 FY2026 collapse of four end markets into one. Restructuring is close to annual: charges in every year from FY2016 to FY2026 totalling about $1.4bn against cumulative GAAP operating income of $26.8m over the decade. Under a technology gap it buys. Under a competitive attack it asserts incumbency and declines to quantify: the May 2025 answer on 3nm exclusivity ("they simply have no idea what we're doing for our customer") and the September 2025 answer on AWS ("we do not see a revenue hole next year") are both categorical statements without a disclosed number behind them, and the filings do not disaggregate custom, so neither can be checked. Under a windfall it buys back stock and raises the target model.

Episodes the current framing omits. 5G and automotive were two of the three acceleration pillars named in October 2021, with automotive described as "the next $1 billion Ethernet IC market". Carrier revenue peaked at $1,084m in FY2023 and declined to $338m in FY2025; the automotive business was sold in 2025. Neither is mentioned as a growth driver in the FY2027 calls. The gross-margin target has been dropped while the operating-margin target has been kept: October 2018 promised above 66% and October 2021 promised 64–66%, and the 38–40% operating margin from the same 2021 model is still guided to, now expected in Q4 FY2027, six years after it was set.▪

10. Management, incentives and capital allocation

Murphy is ten years into the job and holds both the chair and the chief executive role; a shareholder proposal to require an independent chairman drew 36.9% support at the June 2026 meeting. Every other named executive officer seat has changed hands or changed title since fiscal 2021. Six senior departures are on record since FY2023: Jean Hu (CFO, January 2023, to AMD), Mitchell Gaynor (Chief Administration and Legal Officer, FY2023), Dan Christman (EVP Storage, FY2024), Raghib Hussain (President, Products and Technologies, 2 May 2025, to become CEO of Altera), Willem Meintjes (CFO, mid-June 2026) and Ashish Saran (SVP Investor Relations, retiring April 2027 after eight years). Hussain matters most: he co-founded Cavium, arrived with the 2018 acquisition, ran Products and Technologies from April 2021 and presented the custom-silicon strategy at the April 2024 AI event, then resigned five weeks before the June 2025 investor update at which custom silicon was presented as the principal growth driver. His May 2023 special grant of 249,915 target shares had a three-year minimum vesting condition, so the resignation forfeited the whole award, worth roughly $59m at the 2026-08-17 Form 4 price of $236.08.

Annual incentive. Two six-month performance periods weighted equally, payouts from 0% to 200% of target. The metric weights were reset for fiscal 2026: revenue from 45% to 50%, non-GAAP gross margin from 25% to 15%, non-GAAP operating margin from 30% to 35%. Target levels moved down at the same time, and the proxy states the reason: "The lower gross margin target as compared to the prior year reflected the expected near-term product mix shift and the Company's strategy to drive stronger overall financial performance." The bar moved down further than the outcome did, so the gross-margin leg paid 108.8% of target in the first half of fiscal 2026 against 41% a year earlier, on a metric that declined roughly 2.5 points year over year. Second-half revenue of $4,293m against a $4,101m target scored 193.4%, the fiscal-year corporate achievement was 144.84%, and Murphy's cash incentive was $3,621,000 against a $2,500,000 target. Half the weight is on the top line and 15% on the margin line that the custom mix compresses. Investors raised this in fiscal 2025 and the committee declined to change it: "the ECC determined that, for any given year, it may be in the best interests of the Company and our stockholders to set the target performance levels … at levels that … are lower than the prior year."

The non-GAAP definitions used in the plan exclude stock-based compensation, amortization of acquired intangibles, acquisition and divestiture costs and restructuring. In fiscal 2025 that removed the entire $711.8m restructuring charge from the bonus calculation, and the plan paid 131.2% of target in a year with a GAAP net loss of $885.0m.

Long-term equity. Seventy percent of the CEO's annual equity value is granted as performance stock units, measured on relative total shareholder return against the S&P 500 Index over three years — zero payout at 33 points below the index, 100% at parity, 200% at 33 points above — with an earnings-per-share multiplier of 100% to 150% set against a 20-company custom peer group, capped in combination at 250% of target. Two features are asymmetric: the EPS multiplier can only add, and a negative absolute return still permits a full target payout provided the index declined further. The benchmark choice is the larger design feature. Marvell's own Form 10-K stock performance graph tracks the company against the S&P 500 and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index; the incentive plan uses only the first.

Over five fiscal years Marvell returned 56% while the semiconductor index returned 193%. The fiscal 2024 performance stock units, measured against the S&P 500, "fully vested on April 15, 2026 at a payout level of 196% of target". Broadcom, Marvell's principal named competitor in custom silicon, was removed from the compensation peer group for fiscal 2026 and Arista Networks added.

Two other officers were paid more than the CEO, one of them roughly twice as much. Bharathi received four separate equity grants in one year — the 15 April annual award, a 15 May retention award, a 15 June "core talent" award and a 15 July promotion award — described in the proxy as "one-time awards intended to address specific circumstances." One year earlier, in the proxy filed 2025-05-01 responding to a 52% say-on-pay vote, the company had written: "We have not granted one-time equity awards to any NEO since May 2023, and we currently intend to utilize our annual compensation process with respect to changes to our executives' compensation." The May 2025 retention grant was made fourteen days after that statement was filed, and neither the May nor the June grant was promotion-linked; the promotions took effect 15 July 2025.

Say-on-pay support has been 44% (2020), 90%, 93%, 90%, 52% (2024), 83% and 56% (2026) on Marvell's own for-over-for-plus-against convention. Three revolts in seven years, each following a discretionary grant: the 2020 Value Creation Awards, the May 2023 special performance grant, and the fiscal 2026 grant cycle. Fiscal 2026 was the worst relative year of Murphy's tenure — the shares declined 29.8% while the semiconductor index rose 60.8% — and the annual bonus paid 144.84% of target while the board granted $111.5m of stock awards to five officers.

The May 2023 grant is now large. At fiscal 2026 year end three of the four price hurdles had been met and 706,452 shares had been earned by Murphy, with a further 196,235 target shares tied to the remaining $120 tranche. At the 2026-08-17 Form 4 price of $236.08 the earned portion alone is worth $166.8m [estimate: 706,452 earned shares at the disclosed Form 4 execution price]. The fiscal 2026 grants, struck at roughly $52.95 per share in April 2025, include 2,238,045 maximum performance shares across the five officers, worth $528m at the same price against $111.5m of reported grant-date fair value [estimate: proxy maximum share counts at the 2026-08-17 Form 4 price]; the maximum requires both the relative-TSR leg at its 200% cap and the EPS multiplier at 150%, and the TSR leg is measured against the S&P 500 in April 2028.

Insider ownership and trading. All thirteen directors and executive officers together held 1,046,798 shares at 2026-01-31, 0.12% of shares outstanding; Murphy's 412,871 shares were 0.049%. Across 465 Forms 4 between 2021-04-21 and 2026-08-17, Murphy sold 763,500 shares for $55.3m and bought 26,600 for $2.06m; Koopmans sold 224,319 for $22.1m; Bharathi sold 132,337 for $16.2m; Hussain sold 716,939 for $51.6m before leaving. Three patterns point in different directions. Selling followed a fixed schedule and then decelerated: Murphy sold 30,000 shares near the fifteenth of most months from mid-2021 to May 2024, stopped for twenty-two months, resumed at 30,000 in March 2026 at $98.70, then cut to 7,500 a month from April 2026 and held that rate while the price moved from $134.46 to $236.08. Four officers bought on the same day near the low: on 2025-09-25 Murphy bought 13,600 shares at $77.09 and three colleagues bought a further 13,600 between them, about $2.1m in total, and these plus one earlier Murphy purchase are the only officer purchases in the five-year record. And Bharathi, who received the largest package in the company at $46.2m of grant-date value, holds 57,139 shares directly after selling 122,550 shares for $15.6m in the first half of 2026; the three-times-salary guideline is $2.31m, which that holding clears at any price above $41.

Candor. Marvell answers hostile questions and uses customer confidentiality as the boundary. On the Q4 fiscal 2025 call an analyst put the Amazon socket dispute directly — "it doesn't seem like both sides could be correct" — and Murphy engaged, granted the constraint, and made a falsifiable claim about market structure: "it's ourselves in one other very large competitor of ours that can service that market. So these sockets are very sticky. At the same time, each generation, you've got to go bid and you've got to go compete." Four disclosures have since stopped: AI revenue in dollars, quarterly enterprise networking and carrier revenue, the four-way end-market split, and the 64–66% gross-margin target, which was last restated on 2023-05-25 and has never been withdrawn.

Cash acquisitions were the largest single use of cash at 83% of ten-year operating cash flow, and in the three years they were material they exceeded that year's operating cash flow outright: 444% in FY2019, 297% in FY2020 and 434% in FY2022. The gap was funded with $9,433m of debt issuance and $4,340m of divestiture proceeds.

Buyback price sensitivity is partial. Every year's repurchases are above water, and the aggregate 106.9m shares repurchased for $4,233m at a $39.58 average is worth $23,166m at $216.62, 5.5x cost. Exactly $200.0m was spent in six of the last eight quarters, at average prices from $73.09 to $146.58. The two exceptions both followed a divestiture or an authorization increase: Q1 FY2026's step-up to $340m at a $60.48 average came six weeks after the Infineon sale was announced, and Q3 FY2026's $1,300m, including a $1.0bn accelerated repurchase executed 2025-09-24, came after that sale closed and the board added $5.0bn of authorization. The two highest prices Marvell has paid both followed a sharp rally: 1.7m shares at $116.53 in December 2024 and January 2025, immediately before a quarter in which the average price was $60.48; and 1.4m shares at $146.58 between 2026-03-29 and 2026-05-02, immediately after the NVIDIA partnership announcement, into a rally that took the price from $107.11 on 2026-04-04 to $165.15 by 2026-04-30. Half the buyback dollars in the entire ten-year record were spent in FY2026 alone, and 65% in FY2025 and FY2026 together, so the 5.5x outcome is a short-dated result on a long-dated programme.

The buyback has not reduced the share count. Shares outstanding went from 502.4m (FY2017) to 847.3m (2026-01-31), and $4,233m retired 106.9m shares against gross issuance of about 448m. Two stock-funded acquisition years account for +333.9m of the +344.9m increase: the Cavium year added 162.6m and the Inphi and Innovium year 171.3m. Everything else — nine years of vesting, employee stock purchases and options net of 93.7m shares of buyback — nets to about +11m. FY2026 was the one year the count declined, from 866.0m to 847.3m, and that decline lasted ten days: 26.6m shares repurchased in FY2026 at an average $76.46, then 24.5m issued for Celestial AI at an implied $78.73 and 2.1m for XConn at $80.43, in the first ten days of FY2027.▪ The net share-count effect across the two fiscal years is nil, against $2,040m of repurchases and $1,552m of acquisition cash.

Cash spent purely on managing the count is rising fast. Buyback plus tax withheld on net share settlement was $373.7m in FY2024, $999.9m in FY2025, $2,280.8m in FY2026 (130% of operating cash flow, funded partly from the Infineon proceeds) and $765.2m in the first half of FY2027. Withholding alone rose 3.6x year over year in the half, to $365.2m, which is the direct cash cost of settling roughly the same number of vesting units at a share price that has roughly tripled.

Per-share compounding is roughly half of enterprise compounding.

Roughly 6.5 points of annual revenue growth and 7.4 points of annual free-cash-flow growth were absorbed by share issuance. The first half of FY2027 improves the slope: free cash flow per share of $1.08 for the half annualizes to roughly $2.13 on the 900m basic count management guided for Q3, against $1.62 for FY2026.

Capex and the commitments beside it. Property and equipment at 2026-01-31 was $2,342.6m gross and $935.0m net, of which machinery and equipment was $1,825.2m — test, emulation and design infrastructure tied to programme count. Capex was 6.1% of revenue in FY2024, 4.9% in FY2025, 4.3% in FY2026 and 5.5% in the first half of FY2027, where $282.4m was 70% above the prior-year half and annualizes to roughly $565m. Using depreciation of property and equipment as a maintenance proxy, FY2026 splits roughly $222m maintenance and $132m growth [estimate: PP&E depreciation treated as maintenance capex; the proxy is crude for equipment whose life is set by the tape-out cycle, so treat the growth share as $100m–$150m]. The larger commitment is off the capex line: $2,665.8m of unconditional purchase commitments with $1,871.8m due inside FY2027, $635.3m of technology services and licence fees, $152.0m of capital-expenditure commitments, and roughly $1bn of capacity prepayments management forecast for FY2027.

One capex-adjacent write-off is disclosed. A ten-year technology licensing agreement signed in September 2021 was ceased for use in Q3 FY2025 under the restructuring, producing $159.0m of impairment on capitalized licences plus $97.8m of charges for payment obligations, with $268.5m of fees still payable quarterly over the remaining contract term.

The dividend has been $0.06 a quarter since fiscal 2015. Twelve consecutive years without an increase; total dividend dollars rose 68% from FY2017 to FY2026 and all of it came from a 67% larger share count. At $216.62 the yield is 0.11%. Management's own language treats it as fixed: "Maintain current dividend" [deck: 2021-10-06, slide 123].

11. M&A, divestitures and deal track record

A gap that bears on this section: no deal-level return record exists. Marvell has never impaired goodwill, because it tests goodwill as a single reporting unit whose fair value is "our market capitalization as determined through quoted market prices" (10-K FY2026), so the annual test is in practice a share-price test and six loss-making years produced no impairment. Synergy realization was never reported against target after the initial 18-month windows, and no acquisition's revenue is separately disclosed after its first year. The transaction record and the balance-sheet consequences are established; the return on each deal is not.

Marvell is a serial acquirer that spends more than it earns on deals, and the ledger says so plainly. Cash acquisitions of $7,398m equal 83% of ten-year operating cash flow, and the stock consideration on top took the share count from 502m to 847m. What the record establishes is that the acquisitions bought the franchises the company now depends on, and that the prices paid have not yet been earned back at the consolidated level: FY2026 return on invested capital was 7.4% as reported and 25.3% excluding the $11,062m of goodwill those deals created. Two divestitures returned $4,340m of cash and produced the only two years of meaningful GAAP net income in the decade.

What the record supports. Three of the acquisitions built businesses that exist and can be sized. Inphi at 14.5x trailing revenue converted a $683m revenue base into an estimated $3,050m interconnect line by FY2026 and a guided $5,500m–$5,800m by FY2027, so the growth case worked; the return case clears a 10–12% hurdle only from FY2027 onward, because the $11,424m paid for Inphi, Innovium and Aquantia equals 73% of FY2026 invested capital. Avera at $594m is the origin of a franchise management now targets above $10bn a year, having been presented on the May 2019 call as "approximately $300 million in revenue… in the first full year post close." Cavium's contribution is harder to separate, because part of its design capability migrated into the custom platform and part of it is in the communications segment that has since been defunded.

What the record does not support. Synergy realization is unverifiable. Cavium's target was raised from $150–175m to $200m of run-rate cost synergies within eighteen months and Inphi's was $125m; neither was subsequently reported against. The FY2025 restructuring impaired acquired intangibles and purchased technology licences inside $711.8m of charges after a discounted-cash-flow test, and the note lists asset categories without naming the acquired franchises written down, so whether Innovium or Aquantia intangibles were inside it cannot be established. And no goodwill impairment has ever been taken against $11,062m of goodwill at 2026-01-31 or $13,874m at 2026-08-01, which under Marvell's single-reporting-unit test would require the whole company's market capitalization to fall below its book value.▪

The round trip that can be traced. Marvell paid $502m for Aquantia in 2019, whose multi-gigabit Ethernet portfolio included automotive content, and sold the automotive Ethernet business to Infineon for $2,500m in 2025 at roughly 10x revenue. The automotive line also included Marvell's own Brightlane products, so the proceeds cannot be attributed to Aquantia alone. What is established is the pattern: the sub-franchise Infineon described as holding a number-one position with eight of the top ten global OEMs and a $4bn design-win pipeline growing at an expected 25% CAGR is the one Marvell exchanged for cash to fund data center.

Changes in deal terms. The two most recent acquisitions moved from fixed consideration to contingent structures marked against Marvell's own share price. The Celestial earnout was recorded at $315.8m of fair value on 2026-02-02 and remeasured to $647.6m at 2026-05-02, a $331.8m non-cash charge in one quarter and $433.7m across the half; it is a Level 3 Monte Carlo valuation whose inputs include Marvell's share price, so good news about Marvell increases the reported cost of the deal. A cash-settled forward stock purchase contract with a $300.0m notional and a twelve-month term was bought in April 2026 to offset part of that exposure, producing a $131.0m unrealized gain in the half, against maximum settlement of roughly $233.0m of cash and 22.4m shares and an earnout running to FY2029. Purchase-accounting effects from the two February 2026 closings cut GAAP earnings per share to $0.04 in Q1 FY2027 from $0.46 the prior quarter.

The pattern across nine years is consistent: under a technology gap Marvell buys the company that has it, pays in stock when the stock is strong, and accepts the goodwill. Celestial AI in 2026 repeats it at $3,537m for a business whose "revenue and earnings since the acquisition date were not material."

Principal-weighted, at 2026-05-02; net carrying amount $4,961.3m after $38.6m of unamortized discount and issuance cost. The effective rate takes the two 2028 tranches at the 4.964% midpoint because their split is not disclosed. Q2 FY2027 interest expense of $61.6m annualizes to $246.4m, or 4.93% on the stack, above the 4.65% effective rate because the income-statement line also includes interest on technology licence obligations and leases — FY2026 makes the gap explicit at $187.3m of debt interest in Note 7 against $202.6m of interest expense on the face of the income statement.

Nothing matures before February 2028. The largest year is fiscal 2029 at $1,249.9m, 25% of the stack, against $3,932.8m of cash at 2026-08-01 and a $1.5bn undrawn revolver. That wall blends to 3.42%; refinancing it at the 5.30% marginal rate set in April 2026 adds about $24m a year, and repricing the 2031 notes alongside it adds about $42m a year in total against first-half FY2027 operating income of $799.1m.

The $1.5bn revolving credit facility, amended and restated 2025-06-30 with a five-year term, is undrawn and contains the only maintenance covenant in the structure, a maximum leverage ratio tested quarterly. Marvell was in compliance at both disclosed dates; the covenant level is in the June 2025 credit agreement exhibit. The notes include limitations on liens, sale-leaseback transactions and mergers, with no financial maintenance covenant, and a change-of-control repurchase event requires both a change of control and a downgrade below investment grade.

Marvell had no debt until the Cavium acquisition. Deleveraging since FY2025 came from the $2,479m of Infineon proceeds and from EBITDA recovery and not from repayment: gross debt rose from $4,090.5m to $4,999.9m across the same period. Interest coverage on GAAP operating income was 6.5x in FY2026 and 7.5x in Q2 FY2027. Ratings are Baa2 at Moody's, upgraded from Baa3 on 2025-12-17 with a stable outlook, and BBB at S&P, upgraded from BBB- in October 2025 with the outlook revised to positive in July 2026 [web]. The Moody's rationale cited debt to EBITDA declining "from the mid-3x range at FYE 2025 to 1.8x at FQ3 2026" and projected FY2027 revenue "approaching $10 billion" against the approximately $12bn management guided on 2026-08-27.

Obligations outside the debt line. Four items totalling $1,451m are outstanding at 2026-05-02:

  • Technology licence obligations of $245.2m, paid quarterly and classified as financing outflows ($128.3m in FY2026, $56.6m in the first half of FY2027), including $268.5m of remaining fees on the ceased September 2021 licence.
  • Operating lease liabilities of $315.9m on a 7.0-year weighted-average term at a 4.6% discount rate. There is no defined-benefit pension anywhere in the structure.
  • Celestial contingent consideration of $647.6m.
  • Restructuring liabilities of $242.0m.

Beyond them are $2,756.8m of purchase commitments to foundries and test partners with $2,265.2m due in the remainder of FY2027, and $870.0m of wafer and substrate deposits committed as a subsequent event, payable quarterly from Q2 FY2027 through Q2 FY2028. That is a new fixed five-quarter cash call equal to about 17% of the debt stack, and it is not on the balance sheet.

The Q2 FY2027 step-up is the largest single change in the balance sheet. Stock compensation of $326.2m was 112% above the prior-year quarter and 57% above Q1 against revenue growth of 37% and 13%; first-half expense of $533.8m was 81% above the prior-year half. The acquired equity plans explain a slice: Celestial's assumed awards included $190.1m of post-combination expense over three-to-four-year vesting and XConn's $15.0m, so $205.1m spread over three to four years is $50m–$70m a year, under a tenth of the year-on-year quarterly increase. The rest is refresh and retention equity written at a much higher share price, plus headcount. Unamortized expense already committed at 2026-01-31 was about $1.16bn before any FY2027 grant.

The reported diluted count already moves fast. Q1 FY2027 diluted was 893.3m with an 11.3m spread over basic; Q2 FY2027 was 921.2m with a 23.8m spread. The spread doubled in one quarter because the treasury-stock method rewards a rising share price and the $87.77 and $87.00 customer warrants moved deep into the money. Management guides 900m basic and 921m diluted for Q3 FY2027, +5.9% on FY2026's 869.7m diluted in under two years.

Structural risks, ordered by the size of the claim on shareholders.

  1. Equity issuance. 124.6m shares of potential dilution, a stock-compensation run rate that more than doubled to $326.2m in a quarter, and $765.2m spent in the first half of FY2027 on buyback plus withholding to hold the count roughly flat. The three largest claims — the Google warrant, the Celestial earnout and the NVIDIA preferred — were all created in the six months to 2026-08-18.
  2. Contingent consideration marked to Marvell's own share price. A $647.6m liability from a $315.8m starting point, $433.7m of first-half charges, maximum settlement of $233.0m of cash and 22.4m shares, hedged to only $300.0m of notional for twelve months against an earnout running to FY2029.
  3. Supply-chain prepayments. $870.0m of deposits committed in quarterly instalments through Q2 FY2028, on top of $2,265.2m of remaining-FY2027 foundry purchase commitments. These are fixed cash calls with no revenue attached if demand disappoints, against $1,396m of FY2026 free cash flow and $3,932.8m of cash.
  4. Refinancing. The exposure is small: no maturity before February 2028, $1,249.9m in fiscal 2029, and about $39m a year of extra interest if the two tranches issued in 2021 reprice at 5.30%.
  5. Covenant proximity. The undrawn revolver contains one maximum leverage ratio and the level is undisclosed. At 1.1x gross agency-style leverage with $3.9bn of cash, a breach is not a plausible near-term path.
  6. Factoring withdrawal. $735.5m of FY2026 receivable sales run through an uncommitted facility whose termination the company names as a risk to operating results and cash flows.
  7. Floating-rate exposure, structural subordination and currency mismatch. None exists. All sales and most expenses are dollar-denominated, all debt is dollar-denominated and all notes rank pari passu.

13.4 What drove the numbers

Gross margin, FY2025 to FY2026. GAAP gross margin rose 9.7 points and almost none of it came from the product.

Driver FY2025 FY2026 Contribution
Restructuring inside cost of goods sold $357.9m (6.2% of revenue) $0.5m +6.2 pts
Amortization of acquired intangibles inside cost of goods sold $721.7m (12.5%) $639.0m (7.8%) +4.7 pts
Stock-based compensation inside cost of goods sold $47.3m (0.8%) $49.2m (0.6%) +0.2 pts
Underlying product margin (non-GAAP) 61.0% 59.5% (1.5) pts
Total 41.3% 51.0% +9.7 pts

The four contributions sum to 9.6 points against the 9.7-point move; the difference is rounding.

Operating margin, FY2025 to FY2026. The 28.6-point move breaks into +9.7 points of gross margin, +5.9 points from restructuring in operating expenses declining from $353.9m to $15.5m, +8.5 points of R&D leverage as the ratio went from 33.8% to 25.3% of revenue, and +4.5 points of selling and administrative leverage from 13.8% to 9.4%. R&D dollars grew 6.4% while revenue grew 42.1%.

Price against volume. Marvell disclosed an average-selling-price and unit decomposition in the MD&A through the FY2022 10-K and then stopped. The disclosed series: FY2018 ASP +1% on units +4%; FY2019 +23% on units −5%; FY2020 +11% on units −19%; FY2021 +30% on units −20%; FY2022 +20% on units +30%. Unit shipments declined in three of those five years while ASP rose 11%–30%, which is the mix effect of exiting consumer and low-end lines and adding Cavium, Avera and Aquantia content. That decomposition has no successor in the FY2023 through FY2026 filings.

Cash conversion. Cumulative free cash flow of $7,199m across the decade against cumulative GAAP net income of $1,937m is a 3.7x ratio, and the difference is $6,169m of acquired-intangible amortization plus $3,680m of stock-based compensation added back. Days sales outstanding went from 65 to 97 in FY2026 as receivables grew $1,158m against $2,427m of revenue growth, and days payable went from 67 to 98; both are period-end artifacts of a year whose revenue concentrated in its last two months. The cash conversion cycle was 126 days in FY2026 against 149 in FY2023 and 63 in FY2017. Capital intensity roughly tripled across the decade, from 1.6%–2.6% of revenue in FY2017–FY2019 to 4.3%–6.1% in FY2024–FY2026, with capital expenditure at or above depreciation since FY2024.

Leverage. No debt existed until the Cavium acquisition in FY2019. Net debt to EBITDA peaked at 4.9x in FY2025, when EBITDA was compressed by restructuring, and reached 0.7x in FY2026 and 0.36x on the Q2 FY2027 trailing figure. That came from the Infineon proceeds and from EBITDA recovery: gross debt rose from $4,064m to $4,963m over the same period.

Six changes stand out:

  • Data-center concentration rose in every period and reached 79.3% of revenue in the latest quarter.
  • Non-GAAP gross margin has declined in every period since FY2023 and is guided to 57.5%–58.5% for Q3 FY2027, so the acceleration in revenue and the erosion in product margin are the same event.
  • R&D intensity reached its lowest ratio in the ten-year series in FY2026 and has already turned back up, with dollars growing 43% year over year in Q2 FY2027 against 37% revenue growth, while 2nm and 1.4nm tape-outs are funded across a widening programme count.
  • Customer concentration rose in every year of the disclosed series without exception.
  • Inventory days improved from 126 at FY2026 year end to 97 in the latest quarter while purchase commitments to foundries and test partners rose 63% year over year.
  • Customer-warrant vesting reached 0.7m of the 4.2m FY2025 warrant shares at 2026-01-31, roughly fourteen months into a sixty-month term, against 1.0m at a straight-line pace, though that warrant's tranche schedule is not disclosed.

Three metrics were discontinued and are shown here through their last disclosure. The four-way end-market split ended with FY2025 (enterprise networking $626.4m, carrier $338.2m, consumer $316.1m, automotive and industrial $322.4m), removing the ability to check enterprise, carrier and consumer guidance against outcomes. The average-selling-price and unit decomposition ended with the FY2022 10-K. And AI revenue in dollars, given as approximately $200m for FY2023, "over 10% of total company revenue" for FY2024 and "substantially above our $1.5 billion target" for FY2025, was replaced from Q1 FY2026 by "AI now represents the majority of our data center revenue" and then by the custom-versus-interconnect framing, with no FY2026 figure given.

Two new lines have short histories and matter forward. Custom silicon revenue exists only as call commentary and only for three years. And Google warrant tranche vesting, which begins in Q3 FY2027, will report cumulative Google custom-product revenue at $500m per tranche in each subsequent equity note, which is the only externally visible meter on the largest custom relationship.

How consensus got here. The street was cutting through calendar 2025: FY2028 revenue consensus declined from $11,945m in January 2025 to $10,986m in September 2025, and FY2029 from $14,689m to $12,982m. From December 2025 the direction reversed and did not pause, and each step change lands on a reporting date. FY2029 revenue consensus rose 98% between September 2025 and the run date, and FY2029 non-GAAP EPS rose 106%.

The near years are not an opinion. A 2.2% coefficient of variation on FY2027 revenue across 47 estimates, and 0.8% across 29 estimates for the December quarter, describes a panel that has copied a guided number. FY2028 disagreement is entirely about margin: the revenue low is 8.3% below the mean while the operating-profit low is 42.3% below it, so at least one contributor models FY2028 operating margin near 24.8% against a mean of 39.4% and management's 38%–40% target. The distribution is one-sided, and the downside case is invisible in the revenue distribution. Beyond FY2029 the panel thins to five and then four estimates, with a 22.3% revenue coefficient of variation for FY2031.

Where management and the street interpret the same agreement differently. Management's framing of the Google relationship on 2026-08-27 was that the number is real and back-loaded: "There's a lot of upside bias in those numbers in fiscal '29 and beyond in custom", and on an analyst's $120bn arithmetic, "Your math is not wrong. It's just a monster number" [web]. Morgan Stanley's note the following day took the opposite position on incrementality, arguing the Google relationship "had already been incorporated into Marvell's prior forecasts" and that "fundamentals are accelerating, but expectations already appear high", on an Equal-weight rating [web]. Goldman Sachs held a Neutral rating on the same day. The panels also differ on the current year: Bloomberg's post-print FY2027 revenue consensus is $11,861m against stockanalysis.com's $11.56bn on a page dated the same day, which matches Bloomberg's pre-print snapshot, so at least one panel is stale.

What no external source appears to model. The Google warrant is contra-revenue and its rate is calculable at 4.7%–8% of qualifying revenue (§1.1). On $5bn of FY2029 Google revenue that is $235m–$400m of revenue and, because it lands entirely in gross profit, $0.23–$0.40 of FY2029 EPS. Whether the 47 revenue estimates are gross or net of it is not observable from the consensus series, and nine calendar days separated the 8-K from the print.

Marvell's own guidance record separates cleanly into two horizons. The one-quarter number is reliable to about a point: revenue landed at or above the guided midpoint in 20 of 21 quarters, median beat +1.0%, one miss of 1.5%; non-GAAP EPS landed inside the guided range in 21 of 21. The multi-year model is where the misses are, and they are concentrated in margin. Against the 2018, 2020 and 2021 long-term models, revenue targets were met or beaten every time; gross-margin targets were missed every time and by a widening amount — 4.5 to 6.5 points against the 2021 model — and the free-cash-flow target was missed in every year since FY2020.▪ The forecast method extrapolates the current order book, which is why it was too low through an accelerating cycle and too high through a decelerating one. The guided revenue band widened from ±3% to ±5% in December 2022 and has stayed there for fifteen quarters, so the range is now about six times the median beat.

Prices are Bloomberg closes. The perfect-foresight forward multiple divides the fiscal-year-end close by the next fiscal year's actual non-GAAP EPS, so it uses hindsight. The consensus forward multiple is Bloomberg's blended twelve-month-forward figure at the month end nearest each fiscal year end. The non-GAAP EPS column for FY2017 through FY2021 is low confidence: two Bloomberg adjusted-earnings fields disagree for those years and neither the archived 10-Ks nor the archived investor-day transcripts state a non-GAAP figure; from FY2022 the two series agree with management's reported non-GAAP exactly.

Marvell reported a GAAP diluted loss in six of the ten years, and two of the four positive years were disposal-driven. FY2020's $2.34 included $1,123m of other income and a $786m tax benefit on the Wi-Fi sale against a $243m operating loss, and FY2026's $3.07 included the $1.8bn Infineon gain recorded below operating income. FY2026 was the first year in the decade in which GAAP and non-GAAP EPS came within 10% of each other, and the gap closed because of a divestiture gain and not because the adjustments shrank. On consensus the gap persists forward: FY2027E GAAP EPS of $2.10 against non-GAAP $4.17 puts the same $216.62 price at 103x GAAP and 52.0x adjusted, a 1.98x ratio that is the fourth widest of the 45 comparable rows with both multiples and the widest among the named silicon competitors.

Price to book describes acquisition history more than asset value: goodwill of $11,062.2m and acquired intangibles of $1,754.7m at 2026-01-31 make up $12,817m of $14,308.4m of book equity, so tangible book was about $1.5bn. Current price-to-book is 10.5x against a 2015–2026 monthly median of 2.5x and a range of 1.0x to 14.3x.

Revenue exceeded the guidance midpoint in 12 of 12 quarters, by a mean of +1.3% and never by less than +0.3% or more than +4.6%; non-GAAP EPS met or beat the midpoint in 12 of 12. The share reaction bears little relation to any of that: seven of the twelve next sessions were negative, the mean reaction was −1.6%, the mean absolute move was 11.9%, and eleven of twelve moved more than 5%. The next quarter's implied sequential revenue guide correlates 0.51 with the reaction, so it explains roughly a quarter of the variance.

Quarter Reaction What the market reacted to
Q3 FY2024 −5.3% A Q4 guide of $1.42bn against a $1.419bn print, no sequential growth, even though data center revenue of $556m came in "well above our guidance, driven by stronger than forecasted AI revenue"
Q4 FY2024 −11.4% A Q1 guide of $1.15bn, a 19% sequential decline, after a record $765m data center quarter. Enterprise networking, carrier, consumer and storage were correcting at once
Q1 FY2025 −10.5% Data center set a record $816m "well above our guidance", and the Q2 guide of $1.25bn still left the company below the year-ago quarter. The non-AI half was shrinking faster than AI was filling it
Q2 FY2025 +9.2% A Q3 guide of $1.45bn, +13.9% sequential, with data center guided "much higher than that with AI driving it" and Q4 flagged as "extremely strong in data center and AI"
Q3 FY2025 +23.2% Revenue $66m above the guide midpoint and a Q4 guide of $1.8bn, +18.7% sequential. Data center grew 98% year over year to 72% of revenue against 39% a year earlier
Q4 FY2025 −19.8% A record quarter and a Q1 guide of $1.875bn under a buyside bar near $2bn, with "the on-premise portion of our data center end market" guided to a seasonal sequential decline. Concerns about AWS second-sourcing the next Trainium generation ran alongside
Q1 FY2026 −5.6% A Q2 guide of $2.0bn, +5.5% sequential, and an unresolved exchange on 3nm exclusivity in which Murphy conceded it is "certainly possible and likely that customers and our customer may be pursuing multiple paths"
Q2 FY2026 −18.6% Data center revenue of $1.49bn against a consensus near $1.51bn and a Q3 guide implying data center flat sequentially, which Murphy attributed to "nonlinear" custom growth and "lumpiness" in hyperscaler demand
Q3 FY2026 +7.9% FY2027 raised from ~$9.5bn to ~$10bn and FY2028 set at ~$13bn, with data center growth indexed to cloud capex "expected to grow 18% next year"
Q4 FY2026 +18.4% FY2027 raised to approaching $11bn, FY2028 set at ~$15bn with non-GAAP EPS "well over $5", and interconnect FY2027 growth raised from 30% to more than 50%
Q2 FY2027 −10.3% A beat and a raise, FY2027 to ~$12bn and FY2028 to ~$18bn, alongside a Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guide of 57.5%–58.5% against 58.9% delivered, attributed to the custom ramp and expected to persist into Q4. Communications and other declined 3% sequentially, the first sequential decline of the recovery

Fiscal years are calendarised so that an issuer whose fiscal year ends in January through March has fiscal year N+1 mapped to calendar year N, and the Fiscal Year End column discloses each issuer's month so the mapping is checkable per row. Universe order: the subject; the twenty members of the fiscal 2026 compensation peer group from the proxy filed 2026-05-13; named competitors and adjacent public comparables; the optics and packaging value chain; two quality benchmarks; then the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100. 17. Forward model summary

The model runs from revenue to free cash flow for FY2027E through FY2033E, with no multiples, no discounting and no per-share value. The terminal year is FY2033 because the Google warrant's vesting window ends there.

Because Marvell reports one segment, the model is built on five revenue sub-lines that sum to filed FY2026 net revenue exactly, with franchise gross margins solved so they reproduce filed FY2026 product cost. The FY2026 base: custom silicon $1,500.0m at 38.0%, interconnect and electro-optics $2,880.0m at 65.0%, merchant Ethernet switching $320.0m at 68.0%, storage and on-premise compute $1,400.3m at 58.0%, communications and other $2,094.3m at 67.0%, totalling $8,194.6m at 59.5%. Gross profit sums to $4,875m against the $4,876m implied by the reported non-GAAP gross margin, and the same franchise margins applied to the FY2025 mix reproduce the realized FY2025-to-FY2026 incremental gross margin of 55.9%. That identity is a consistency check and not independent evidence: the merchant margins were chosen so it would close, and the two communications gross-margin estimates differ, at 58%–60% against 66%–71%.

FY2027 is half reported. First-half revenue was $5,157m, Q3 is guided to $3,150m ±5%, and the base implies a Q4 of $3,673m, 16.6% above the Q3 guide midpoint against consensus of $3,643m. FY2028 revenue of $17,787m is management's own ~$18bn; the departure from consensus is below the revenue line, at 56.0% non-GAAP gross margin against consensus 58.0% and non-GAAP EPS of $6.17 against $6.67.

Why the margin declines while revenue accelerates. Custom goes from 18.3% of FY2026 revenue to 33.6% of FY2029 revenue and 35.1% by FY2033. At a 38% custom gross margin against 63%–65% in interconnect, every point of custom mix costs roughly 0.26 points of blended gross margin, and adding roughly half a point a year of price erosion in interconnect and switching takes the blend from 59.5% to 54.3% by FY2029 and 52.3% by FY2033.▪ Operating margin holds near 37% because operating expense grows at 0.74x the revenue growth rate, falling from 24.2% of FY2026 revenue toward a 16.2% floor. Incremental non-GAAP operating margins run 41.1%, 38.9%, 35.7%, 35.6%, 35.1%, 34.0% and 31.8% across the seven years. Every one is below the 50.5% realized in FY2026, the best in the record.

The bear is not a revenue collapse: revenue still compounds 16.6% a year to $24,029m. It is gross margin decaying 1.5 points a year while operating expense has a floor, so non-GAAP operating income peaks at $5,073m in FY2032 and non-GAAP EPS peaks at $4.34 in FY2028 before declining to $3.72. Incremental non-GAAP operating margin is 22.3% in FY2028 and around zero from FY2029, and the free-cash-flow margin runs 11%–15%. In the bull case non-GAAP gross margin still declines, to 55.2%, because custom mix rises in every scenario; the free-cash-flow margin reaches 30.6%, the first time in any scenario that the above-30% target present in every long-term model since 2018 is met.

Against the base-rate distribution, the base case three-year revenue CAGR of 41.8% is above the 90th percentile for US-listed semiconductor companies at this scale (29.3%) and below the single best three-year observation on record (51.9%, AMD FY2019–FY2022). Conditioned on a hot starting year, which is Marvell's condition after +42.1% in FY2026, the best observation in the reference class is 32.4% and the median is 8.8%, so the base case exceeds every conditional precedent. The bear at 27.8% over three years is close to the unconditional 90th percentile.

Interconnect dominates because it is the largest revenue line and carries a high margin. At 64.5% in FY2027 it is not the highest — merchant Ethernet switching and communications are both modelled at 67.0% — but it is much the largest, so an eight-point move in its growth rate compounds over six years into a swing roughly the size of the whole of FY2026 revenue.▪ The growth case is narrated around custom, and custom is the second-largest lever. The ranking inverts in the near years: in FY2029 the custom gross margin swings $800m of operating income against $653m for custom revenue growth, because custom mix rises fastest before the revenue base compounds.

17.4 Assumptions and where each is contested

Several assumptions do not survive scrutiny, and the counter-argument is beside each. The five drivers with the largest effect on the outcome are marked.

Driver Bear Base Bull Basis Where it is contested
Custom revenue growth, FY2027 60% 66% 70% Estimated Refuted. The 60%–70% band excludes management's own written ">20%" guide by a factor of three, so no scenario allows the company's guidance to be right. The band depends on interconnect being pinned at exactly its guided floor of +70%; at +90% the same identity solves with custom near $1,850m. Management has raised interconnect three times and then replaced the number with "continues to lead the way", which is a floor being exceeded. Evidence supports roughly +25% to +75%
Custom revenue growth, FY2028 60% 108.8% 140% Management guide Weak. The multiplier is management's "more than double", but it is applied to a base 30% above management's own. Management's own arithmetic gives $4.0bn–$4.5bn of FY2028 custom; the model gives $5,199m. The bear at +60% assumes the new programme slips, when the live event in the record is loss of an existing one
Custom revenue growth, FY2029 21% 53.8% 80% Estimated Weak. FY2029 is the first uncontracted year: purchase orders cover FY2027 and firm volume requirements FY2028, and nothing was said about FY2029. The only listed comparable declined 39% in a single year on exactly this mechanism after +116% and +65%. A 21% floor for an uncontracted year in that reference class understates the downside; the bear should reach a decline
Custom revenue, FY2029 $4,560m $7,848m $10,840m Estimated Weak. The same assumption in dollars. The base at 22% below both management's target and consensus is the model's most defensible departure; the failure is at the bottom, where the bear is +21% growth and not a programme loss
Custom revenue CAGR, FY2029–FY2033 13.7% 14.3% 17.2% Panel base rate Refuted. The cited base rate contradicts the range it justifies: Alchip compounded 31% over 2021–2025 with individual years of +116%, +65% and −39%, and the band here is 3.5 points wide with the bear 0.6 points below the base. A line composed of a handful of single-customer sockets re-competed at each node cannot have a 3.5-point range, because losing one of five sockets removes roughly $2.1bn of socket-year revenue at once. Evidence supports roughly −5% to +25%
Custom gross margin, FY2029 33% 38% 42% Estimated Weak. The figure is a FY2026 solve held flat through a period in which custom revenue rises 5.3x, and the Alchip record says the direction is wrong: its gross margin declined from 34.2% to 19.6% as turnkey production ramped 3.8x. The bear of 33% is also above every observed pure-play production margin (19.6%–26.4% at Alchip, 21.5% at GUC), so it should be 25%–28%, worth roughly $1,300m of FY2029 operating income against the modelled $800m
Google share of custom revenue, FY2029 28% 31% 34% Estimated Refuted. The share is set so that cumulative Google revenue vests a plausible fraction of the warrant, which sets the input to produce the desired output. The commercial agreement is four weeks old at the run date, the 8-K discloses no dollar figure, no volume commitment and no start date, and management declined to size it. One credible external reading puts incremental FY2029 Google revenue near zero. Evidence supports 0% to roughly 50%
Google warrant contra-revenue rate 6.6% 6.0% 4.7% Estimated Weak. The band should shift up. The realized analogue implies about 74% of strike, or roughly $153 per share, a 7.3% rate above the bear. Materiality is small: the driver ranks ninth of eleven on the model's own sensitivity
Interconnect growth, FY2027 68% 70.1% 72% Management guide Weak. The base is the guided floor and half the year is reported, so the base survives; the four-point band does not. Management's figure moved from 30% to above 50% to above 70% across three quarters, then was replaced with words. This driver is also not independent of custom growth: both are solved from the same data-center identity, so a bull on one is arithmetically a bear on the other, and the scenarios move them separately
Interconnect growth, FY2028 38% 51% 60% Management guide Weak. The largest lever in the model. The base is above both external figures: management guides interconnect only to "outpace" cloud capex assumed at 30%-plus, and J.P. Morgan puts CY2027 data-centre capex at +40%. The bear excludes the one event this driver has experienced — the 800G-and-above transceiver market contracted through the CY2023 digestion — and two dated substitutions are live before the modelled year. The range should reach a flat year
Interconnect CAGR, FY2029–FY2033 8.7% 14.7% 17.8% Estimated Weak. The base survives, at roughly the 70th percentile of the panel's five-year distribution at this scale. The bear does not: +8.7% is the panel median applied to the model's most substitution-exposed line, and co-packaged optics does not slow this line, it removes the socket
Interconnect gross margin, FY2027 64% 64.5% 65% Estimated Weak. The stated rationale and the value disagree — the justification puts interconnect at the top of the segment while the model places switching a further 2.5 points above it. The underlying solve moves 3.3 points on an input nobody outside the company can observe. The honest range is 63%–68%
Interconnect gross-margin erosion 1.5pp 0.5pp 0.2pp Own record Weak. The record cited does not measure this quantity. Consolidated non-GAAP gross margin has declined every year since FY2022, and management and the model both attribute that to custom mix, which the model already captures separately, so using it here double-counts. The only direct price disclosure Marvell ever made runs the other way: ASP rose 1%, 23%, 11%, 30% and 20% across FY2018–FY2022
Merchant switching revenue, FY2028 $850m $1,050m $1,300m Management guide Weak. The base treats an annualized run-rate guide as a full-year figure. Management's words are "more than $1 billion in annualized revenue in fiscal 2028", against explicit full-year framings for FY2026 and FY2027. If $1bn is a Q4 exit rate, the full year is roughly $800m–$870m, which is the model's bear
Merchant switching CAGR, FY2029–FY2033 11.7% 19.1% 27.0% Estimated Weak. The base compounds above its own market. Marvell sizes switch silicon at a 17% CAGR and holds roughly 4%; the base takes share to roughly 11% by FY2029 and 13% by FY2033 against an incumbent above 70%, a path stated nowhere. The driver is defined as a count of qualified platforms, which does not move with market growth, so a smooth CAGR is the wrong shape
Merchant switching gross margin, FY2027 66% 67% 68% Estimated Refuted. The justification cites an incumbent at roughly 96% share; no source supports that for switch silicon, where the incumbent is above 70%, and the 95% figure comes from a different market. The margin is assigned to a line whose unit economics cannot be built from public material, and the competitive position argues the other way: Marvell is the 4%-share second source qualified to obtain price leverage. Evidence supports switching at or below the segment average
Storage growth, FY2027 22% 26.8% 30% Estimated Refuted. The assumption is explicitly the residual that balances the FY2027 data-center guide, and that residual moves from +9% to +71% depending only on where interconnect lands. Every driver-based piece of evidence contradicts +26.8%: Marvell sizes storage at a 9% CAGR, the exposure is drives and not bytes, total HDD units grew 0.4% in CY2025, and the driver is structurally flat units with mid-single-digit content growth. The path is also discontinuous: 26.8% in FY2027 then 6.5% a year for six years. Evidence supports roughly +8% to +15%
Storage CAGR, FY2028–FY2033 1.3% 6.5% 8.4% Panel base rate Holds. The base is 2.5 points below Marvell's own 9% storage market CAGR and built on the correct unit driver. The bear is a six-year average and the bear scenario runs storage at −5% in FY2029 inside it, so a down year is represented
Storage gross margin, FY2027 57% 57.5% 58% Estimated Refuted. The justification states the mechanism: the value is set so the five franchise margins reproduce reported FY2026 gross profit exactly, which is one equation resolved by choosing four of five values. The model's own source puts the nearline controller row at roughly 64% and the residual at roughly 65%, six to seven points higher. Correcting storage forces roughly two points out of interconnect and switching, the two lines that produce the growth
Communications growth, FY2027 1.2% 4.1% 9.8% Estimated Holds. First half is reported at $1,152.9m and Q3 is guided to about $487m, so the base implies a Q4 of $540m, +10.9% sequentially against a nine-quarter maximum of 13.8%, and management has signalled a broad-based Q4 step-up. This is the one revenue assumption where management's own target is the bull case
Communications CAGR, FY2028–FY2033 −0.5% 2.8% 3.7% Panel base rate Weak. The bear is far too shallow. This franchise declined 54% in two years within the last three, the sell-in structure amplifies the underlying equipment markets, both named OCTEON Fusion customers have announced alternatives, consumer is tied to a six-year-old console generation, and enterprise normalised 27% below its FY2023 print. The bear should reach −8% to −10% a year
Communications gross margin, FY2027 66.5% 67% 67.5% Estimated Weak. Two builds disagree by 7 to 13 points on this number and the model resolves it with a one-point band. The margin is also held flat in every year through FY2033 in the franchise where management redirected R&D away and where the divested automotive line ran at roughly 60%. Supportable range 58%–71%
Non-GAAP operating expenses, FY2027 $2,600m $2,560m $2,550m Management guide Holds. Half the year is reported and Q3 is guided at ~$655m, so only Q4 is open. Repeating Q2's 1.8% overrun across the full year gives $2,596m, inside the bear
Operating expense growth as a multiple of revenue growth 1.27x 0.74x 0.71x Estimated Weak. The stated value does not describe the model: computed from the projections the ratio runs 0.56x, 0.74x, 0.74x, 0.89x, 0.97x and 1.06x across FY2028–FY2033, because the later years are governed by the operating-expense floor and not by this multiplier. The bull of 0.71x is also 0.03 below the base while the scenario work uses management's own 0.50x. And a ratio is the wrong shape for a cost base committed against a two-to-three-year design cycle: when revenue declined 7.0% in FY2024, non-GAAP operating income declined 24.0%, a 122% decremental
Operating expenses as % of revenue, FY2033 26.7% 16.2% 14.0% Estimated Weak. The base is below every year in Marvell's record: 32.1% FY2022, 29.0%, 32.2%, 32.1%, 24.2% FY2026, 21.3% guided FY2027. R&D alone was 25.3% of revenue in FY2026 and 27.1% in Q2 FY2027. The panel does contain precedents for a fall to the mid teens at scale, and what it does not address is that custom silicon needs a dedicated design team and mask set per programme, and the model adds programmes every year. The base belongs closer to the bear
Stock-based compensation, % of revenue FY2033 7.8% 5.7% 4.5% Own record Refuted. The record refutes the range: 9.0%, 8.1%, 10.3%, 9.3%, 11.1%, 10.4%, then 7.2% in FY2026, 8.6% in Q1 FY2027 and 11.9% in Q2. The seven-year minimum is 7.2%, so the base is below every observation since FY2019 and the bear exceeds only one of the last seven years. Q2 FY2027 was 112% above the prior-year quarter, and the acquired plans explain $50m–$70m a year of that. Evidence supports 6%–12% with a base near 8%
Diluted shares, FY2029 964m 940m 918m Estimated Weak. The bull is excluded by disclosed guidance: Marvell guides 921m diluted for Q3 FY2027, two fiscal years earlier. The count rose 7.6% in two quarters, the diluted-to-basic spread doubled in one quarter as the customer warrants moved into the money, 124.6m of instruments are outstanding ahead of it, and the buyback has slowed to $400.0m in the first half against $2,040.1m in FY2026. The base belongs near 950m–960m
Diluted share CAGR, FY2027–FY2033 2.5% 1.0% 0.0% Own record Weak. The record supports two numbers and the assumption uses neither: 5.9% a year with deals, roughly 0.15% a year without them, because 333.9m of the 344.9m ten-year increase came from two stock-funded acquisitions. A 1.0% base therefore assumes no stock-funded acquisition across seven years, in a company that issued stock for acquisitions in five of the last nine years and again in the first ten days of FY2027
Non-GAAP tax rate, FY2029 16% 14% 13% Management guide Weak. Management guides 11% for FY2027 and about 13% for FY2028, so FY2029 is unguided and the three-point band extrapolates the least stable line in the record. The foreign incentive runs only to 2030-02-01 with disclosed clawback risk, and profit mix shifts toward US-designed custom silicon. The bear should reach 18%–20%
Interest and other, net, FY2029 $(170)m $(100)m $(40)m Own record Holds. Eight fixed-rate tranches at a 4.65% principal-weighted effective rate, no floating leg, nothing maturing before February 2028, and $1,249.9m repricing in FY2029 adding about $24m a year. The $130m band is wide relative to the remaining uncertainty
Capex, % of revenue FY2029 6.0% 4.6% 4.3% Own record Weak. The base is below the current run rate: 6.1% FY2024, 4.9%, 4.3%, and 5.5% in the first half of FY2027, where capex was 70% above the prior-year half. Outsourced test is a named supply constraint and AI parts need long test times, so test capacity scales with volume. Evidence supports about 5.5% as the base with the bear above 6%

Choosing 28.0% releases $330m–$580m of cash on FY2029 revenue that the balance sheet has not shown, and the risk is one-sided in a supply-constrained ramp. The base belongs at about 30%
