The base matches consensus in FY2027 and FY2028 because both are management's guide and consensus has copied it. The gap opens where nobody has guided, and four mechanisms compound. Gross margin: consensus holds FY2029 at 56.7% while custom grows to roughly 39% of revenue, which requires custom silicon near 50%, against three solves that put it at 30%–44%. Growth shape: consensus runs +45%, +50%, +44% with no decay in a panel where three consecutive years of 40%-plus growth from a $4bn-plus base has happened twice in twenty years and four consecutive years has happened never. Operating expense: backing it out of consensus gives 14.9% of revenue in FY2029 and 12.9% in FY2030, against 24.2% in FY2026 and 21.3% guided for FY2027, while Marvell's own R&D intensity has turned back up. Share count: consensus implies 900.9m diluted shares in FY2029 against 921m guided for Q3 FY2027 and 124.6m of instruments outstanding.

Even the base case requires Marvell to beat its own share target. Marvell sized the CY2028 data-center market at $94bn in June 2025 and set a 20% share target, roughly $18,800m of FY2029 data-center revenue. The base puts FY2029 data center at $21,081m, 22.4% of that market; consensus implies about $23,400m, 24.9%. Both require exceeding the goal set fourteen months earlier, or a third upward revision to the market estimate, which was already raised 25% between April 2024 and June 2025.

18. Risks

Ordered by dollars of FY2028 revenue or gross profit exposed, multiplied by the likelihood the mechanism operates within eight quarters.

R1 — Single-customer custom programmes with no resale market. Custom silicon is designed to one buyer's specification and sold only to that buyer, so a cancelled, re-specified or re-awarded programme does not transfer. The 10-K states it: "there may be no other customers for these products due to their custom or semi-custom nature." A second failure path was added in FY2026 — the customer's own design may underperform even where Marvell executes to specification. Custom was roughly $1.5bn of FY2026 revenue and, on management's growth rates against its own FY2028 revenue guide, roughly $4bn–$5bn of FY2028, about a quarter of the company (§17.4). Concentration around it rose each year from FY2024 to Q1 FY2027: Distributor A from 24% (FY2024) to 45% (Q1 FY2027), Direct Customer A from under 10% to 16%, top-ten customers from 72% to 82%, and three customers at 75% of gross accounts receivable. Leading indicators: the Distributor A and Customer A percentages in each 10-Q; the count of vested Fiscal 2025 warrant shares against the straight-line pace (§13.5); the count of vested Google warrant shares from Q3 FY2027, each of which reports $500m of cumulative custom revenue from that customer; and sequential data-center growth against the guided rate. What reduces the exposure without removing it: the Google agreement spans five product categories, and the warrants vest only against recognized revenue, so a programme that does not ship also does not dilute.

R2 — Take-or-pay supply commitments against cancellable customer orders. Customer orders are cancellable at short notice; Marvell's supply obligations are not, and cancellation of a purchase order "requires payment of all costs and expenses incurred through the date of cancellation." At 2026-05-02, purchase commitments to foundries and test partners were $2,756.8m with $2,265.2m due in the remainder of FY2027, plus $709.3m of technology services and licence fees, $185.5m of capital-expenditure commitments and $870.0m of new wafer and substrate deposits payable quarterly through Q2 FY2028. That is roughly $3.1bn of near-term fixed supply outflow against $1,396m of FY2026 free cash flow and $3,932.8m of cash. The mechanism has run before in reverse: in FY2025 Marvell amended reservation agreements and cut purchase-level commitments from $2.0bn to $544.6m when demand missed, so the agreements bind less than the description implies in both directions. Leading indicators: inventory days; the prepaid-expenses and other-non-current-asset lines where prepayments land, which rose from $247.2m to $407.5m and from $1,726.9m to $2,021.5m between the fiscal year end and 2026-08-01; the size of the next commitment table; and any purchase-commitment loss accrual.

R3 — Gross margin declining as custom mix rises. Custom passes more of the bill of materials through, so it converts revenue to gross profit at a lower rate, and management has said so on the record as the driver of the current guide. Non-GAAP gross margin has declined in each of the last four fiscal years to 58.9% in Q2 FY2027, with 57.5%–58.5% guided for Q3 and the same range indicated for Q4. The incremental gross margin implied by the Q3 guide is 48% to 56% [estimate: guided Q3 revenue at the guided margin band less the Q2 actual, over the revenue increment], three to eleven points below the corporate average. Applying management's own FY2029 target of $10bn-plus of custom revenue moves custom from roughly 18% of revenue toward 40%, pulling the blend toward the incremental figure. Leading indicators: the quarterly gross-margin guide band; the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin; and whether the Investor Day model lowers the gross-margin target while raising the operating-margin target.

R4 — Demand concentrated in hyperscaler AI capital budgets. Data center went from 40% of revenue in FY2024 to 79% in Q2 FY2027, and the FY2028 guide embeds data-center growth above 60%. The 10-K states that "the current level of capital expenditure (capex) on AI infrastructure may not be sustainable over the long term." Three of the four largest buyers are funding the marginal dollar with something other than operating cash (§5). The guide has moved up five consecutive times in eleven months on the same stated evidence base, and the same order-book extrapolation can move it down: FY2027 data-center growth was 25% in December 2025 and 60% in August 2026. Leading indicators: hyperscaler quarterly capex guides; sequential data-center growth against the guided rate; any change in the "more than 60%" FY2028 language; and the Section 232 semiconductor determination.

R5 — Equity issued as customer and technology currency, marked against Marvell's own stock. The customer warrants reduce reported revenue as qualifying revenue is recognized, so the top line absorbs the cost while the dilution runs separately, and the Celestial earnout is remeasured against the share price each quarter. The instruments total roughly 125m potential shares against 900m basic guided for Q3 FY2027. The Celestial liability moved from $315.8m at close to $647.6m at 2026-05-02, hedged to $300.0m of notional for twelve months against an earnout running to FY2029, and both the liability and the hedge are Level 3 valuations using Marvell's own share-price volatility. This risk is self-referential in both directions: a rising share price increases the earnout liability, and a falling price creates a loss on the forward purchase contract and reduces the value of the equity already handed to customers. Both run through other expense and both are excluded from the non-GAAP figures management guides on. Leading indicators: vested warrant share counts in each equity note; the quarterly change in the contingent-consideration liability; the diluted count against the 921m guide; and whether the forward purchase contract is rolled at expiry in April 2027.

R6 — The communications franchise turning down again. The four legacy end markets were consolidated into one line in Q4 FY2026 and had new-product investment cut in the FY2025 restructuring, so the FY2026 recovery came from inventory normalization, which does not repeat. Q2 FY2027 declined 3% sequentially, the first sequential decline of the recovery, and Q3 FY2027 is guided down in the low-to-mid teens both sequentially and year over year, to roughly $480m–$495m. Reaching the "approach our 10% target" full-year figure needs a Q4 of roughly $660m, a 36% sequential increase, and no quarter since the restructuring has printed above $600m. Leading indicators: the Q3 print against the guided decline; the Q4 sequential recovery against that arithmetic; and distributor channel inventory, given sell-in recognition on 43% of FY2026 revenue.

R7 — Supply allocation and the packaging and substrate constraint. Marvell owns no fabs, places firm orders up to 26 weeks ahead and supply commitments up to 52 weeks, and AI accelerators need 2.5D and 3D interposers, high-layer-count substrates and HBM, so the constraint binds at packaging and substrate before wafers. The Q2 FY2027 release added a specific phrase with no precedent in the prior four quarterly releases: "allocation of supply to our competitors." Marvell experienced industry-wide supply constraints in the first quarters of FY2023, and the financial answer to date converts a supply risk into a cash and take-or-pay risk through the deposits in R2. Leading indicators: advanced-packaging capacity commentary from the foundry layer; the size of each successive deposit commitment; whether a quarter's revenue is described as supply-limited; and changes to the disclosed 26-week and 52-week lead times.

R8 — Senior leadership turnover during a two-year revenue doubling. Custom programmes are relationship and execution intensive across multi-year tape-out cycles. The FY2026 10-K names the loss of the former President, Products and Technologies to another semiconductor company; the CFO changed in June 2026 for the second time in three and a half years; and the eight-year investor relations head retires in April 2027. Headcount was 7,480 at 2026-01-31 against 7,448 at FY2023 year end, so a revenue doubling is being attempted without a proportional increase in people, with voluntary turnover of about 7% in FY2026 and a return-to-office policy the 10-K names as a retention challenge. Leading indicators: Section 16 filings and Item 5.02 departures; the human-capital turnover figure in the next 10-K.

R9 — Goodwill and acquired intangibles against a thin tangible equity base. At 2026-08-01 goodwill was $13,873.9m and acquired intangibles $2,346.6m, a combined $16,220.5m of $27,554.6m of total assets and 87.5% of $18,531.6m of stockholders' equity, so tangible equity is roughly $2,311m. Marvell tests goodwill as a single reporting unit against its own market capitalization, so an impairment requires that measure to fall below book value; a demand step-down that triggered it would produce a large equity effect with no cash effect. Amortization of acquired intangibles was $942.0m in FY2026 and is excluded from every non-GAAP figure management guides on. Leading indicators: the annual goodwill test disclosure and any narrowing of headroom; the amortization schedule.

R10 — China and trade policy acting on margin more than on demand. Geographic revenue is reported by destination of shipment, and the 10-K states that a substantial majority of China shipments are for non-China customers with manufacturing inside China, so the 36% China line is mostly contract-manufacturing location. The live exposures are a revenue-share condition on export licences (a 2025 precedent implying 15% of gross China-derived revenue, disclosed as not having impacted Marvell), a January 2026 licensing policy including a 25% tariff, and the April 2025 Section 232 investigation covering substrates and bare wafers. Neither the direct China end-customer revenue nor the fraction of shipments that would fall inside such a regime is disclosed, so the exposure cannot be sized. Leading indicators: the Section 232 determination; licensing policy changes; the destination-of-shipment table each quarter, with Taiwan as the assembly proxy.

R11 — Operating cash flow flattered by non-recourse factoring. Receivables sold without recourse are presented as cash from operations: $335.7m in FY2024, $868.8m in FY2025, $735.5m in FY2026 and $300.9m in Q1 FY2027 alone, against $1,751m of FY2026 operating cash flow. The FY2026 change in factored volume was negative $133.3m, so the FY2026 figure absorbed a headwind from this line; a cessation would be a one-time working-capital outflow of the standing balance. The facility is uncommitted. Leading indicators: the factored-volume disclosure in each Note 2; days sales outstanding against factored volume.

Which risks arrive together. A hyperscaler capital-budget pause moves R4 first, and within one to two quarters pulls in R1 (custom programme volumes with no second buyer), R2 (the near-term purchase commitments and deposits become obligations against falling revenue), R7 (the prepaid supply arrives anyway), R5 (warrant vesting stops and the buyback loses the cash flow that funds dilution management) and R9 (goodwill testing on $13.9bn). R6 offers no offset because communications is already guided down. A socket loss moves R1 and R3 in opposite directions on the income statement: revenue declines while the surviving mix improves gross margin, so a socket loss can print as a margin beat, and the first sign would be data-center growth decelerating while non-GAAP gross margin rises above the guide band.

19. Source disclosure

Filings and archives. Ten 10-K filings covering FY2017 through FY2026, six 10-Qs from calendar 2024-Q3 through 2026-Q2, the Q2 FY2027 8-K earnings release of 2026-08-27, the 8-K of 2026-08-19 recording the Google commercial agreement and warrant, twenty-two quarterly earnings releases with their guidance extracts, and six DEF 14A proxy statements covering fiscal 2021 through fiscal 2026. Because SEC ticker-to-CIK mapping resolves Marvell to the Delaware holdco created in the 2021 redomestication, which has only five 10-Ks, the FY2017 through FY2021 annual reports were fetched separately from the predecessor Bermuda registrant.

Transcripts. Twenty-four earnings calls from Q3 FY2021 (December 2020) to Q2 FY2027 (August 2026), and sixty-seven presentation transcripts from September 2016 to August 2026, including all four analyst and investor days (2017, 2018, 2020, 2021), the M&A calls for Cavium, Aquantia, Avera, Inphi, Innovium and the Infineon divestiture, the April 2024 AI infrastructure update, the June 2025 custom silicon event, the September 2025 hosted special call and the August 2026 Six Five Summit interview. Six presentation dates were corrected against the event date in the title after an enumeration captured a revision date instead, the worst case by 1,466 days.

Decks. Fifteen investor presentations from 2017 to 2026 with 945 rendered slides, spanning two M&A decks, four investor days, two AI investor events, one corporate overview and six quarterly results decks.

Financial and market data. XBRL-derived income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, repurchase and share-count series for FY2020 through FY2026 plus quarterlies; a research database holding Marvell in twelve tables including 1,192 statement-level financial facts, 674 estimate snapshots, 180 fund-holding rows and 71 executive-compensation rows; Bloomberg via xBBG pulled 2026-08-28 for daily prices and total return from 2015-01-02, monthly forward-expectation history, consensus by fiscal year to FY2031, quarterly consensus, estimate dispersion under relative fiscal-period overrides, and the 49-row comparable-company universe; and 465 Forms 4 filed between 2021-04-21 and 2026-08-17.

Peer sources. Filings for Broadcom, NVIDIA, Astera Labs, Credo, MACOM, Semtech, Silicon Motion, Rambus, Cisco, Microchip, NXP, Qualcomm, AMD, Intel, Seagate, TSMC, Micron, Amkor, ASE, Coherent, Lumentum, Fabrinet, Celestica, Jabil, Arista, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta, plus Broadcom's Q4 FY2023 through Q2 FY2026 earnings calls.

Data built from primary sources. A ten-year annual financial series and a twelve-quarter quarterly series reconciled to each year's filed figures to the dollar; a franchise-level revenue and gross-margin reconstruction for FY2026; a seven-year driver-based operating model with 34 assumptions across three scenarios; a market-pricing series covering 2,931 trading sessions with drawdown, rally, fiscal-year return and forward-multiple derivations; and the comparable-company table.

Gaps and failures. Four sources were unavailable and were worked around. No year-over-year textual redline of the ten 10-K filings had been built for Marvell, so the risk-factor and MD&A comparison in §18 was done by extracting Item 1A from each of the ten archived annual reports and diffing them directly. No standardized fundamental workbook exists for Marvell, so the XBRL extracts served as the reported-financials source. No sell-side report covers Marvell as a primary name: a 39-report digest mentions the ticker exactly once, inside a note about Broadcom's ASIC share, so the external-expectations work uses Bloomberg consensus, four industry notes that reference Marvell, and named single-name positions sourced to the trade press. And the external-dataset registry returns one semiconductor dataset for this company, a paid memory-pricing mosaic with no coded connector, described in Appendix C.

Two structural gaps are listed in §20: no deal-level acquisition return record exists, and no franchise-level capital allocation is disclosed.

20. What is still unknown, and what would resolve it

Six gaps are material enough to change the conclusions above, and each has a named metric that would settle it.

  1. The custom silicon gross margin. The single largest swing factor in any FY2029 answer — $800m of operating income for a five-point move — and it has never been disclosed. Single-segment reporting means it cannot be derived from any filing. What would resolve it: a disclosed custom revenue line or franchise margin at the 2026-10-06 Investor Day, or a disaggregation in a future Note 3.
  2. What roughly $22bn of acquisitions returned. Cash acquisitions alone were $7,398m against $8,897m of decade operating cash flow, and no deal-level return, synergy realization or divestiture round-trip can be computed. Marvell tests goodwill as a single reporting unit against its own market capitalization, so the impairment record that would grade the deals will not exist. Cavium's synergy target was raised to $200m and Inphi's set at $125m; neither was reported against after the initial windows. What would resolve it: revenue disclosure for an acquired franchise, or a multi-reporting-unit goodwill structure.
  3. The identity and end-customer mix of Distributor A. At 45% of Q1 FY2027 revenue this is the largest reported relationship in the company, and whether custom silicon ships through it or around it determines whether the accelerating concentration is a custom phenomenon or a merchant one. What would resolve it: a customer-type disaggregation by end market, or an end-customer concentration disclosure.
  4. The Google warrant's grant-date fair value and the revenue it assumes. The contra-revenue rate used here spans 4.7% to 8% of qualifying revenue, and the grant-date fair value spans $6bn to $10bn. Whether the ~$12bn FY2027 and ~$18bn FY2028 revenue figures are stated gross or net of it is also unaddressed, and vesting begins in the quarter now guided at $3,150m. What would resolve it: the Q3 FY2027 10-Q, which will contain the first measurement, and the vested-share count in each subsequent equity note.
  5. What custom silicon earns on the capital it consumes. No franchise-level capital is allocated anywhere, and custom absorbs the $2,665.8m purchase-commitment base, the ~$1bn of FY2027 capacity prepayments, the $870.0m of deposits and roughly 28 cents of working capital per incremental revenue dollar while earning an estimated 26 points less gross margin than merchant. Customer non-recurring engineering, recorded as a reduction of operating expense, is not sized at any level, so custom's operating margin cannot be computed at all. What would resolve it: an NRE disclosure, or capital and operating expense by franchise.
  6. What the FY2029 custom target and the CY2028 share target reconcile to. They cannot both hold alongside the FY2028 guide without the merchant data-center franchises declining 21% to 24% in FY2029 (§8). Management declined to update either on 2026-08-27 and deferred both to the Investor Day.

Six further questions matter less individually and would each move a number.

  • Whether Marvell retains any Trainium content, and what share of custom revenue comes from that relationship. Management has declined the socket question on four consecutive calls.
  • The revenue and growth of the clearance-gated US government and defence ASIC business. It is the only structurally protected position left in the communications segment and its size has never been published.
  • Which sub-franchise produced the Q2 FY2027 sequential decline and the guided Q3 decline in communications. Sub-market reporting ended with the Q3 FY2026 10-Q, so it cannot be derived from filed data.
  • The revenue milestones behind Celestial AI's contingent consideration. The 10-Q describes "specified cumulative revenue milestones through the end of fiscal 2029" without stating the thresholds, against maximum settlement of roughly $233.0m of cash and 22.4m shares and a liability already written up $433.7m in one half-year.
  • How much revenue the FY2025 cancelled product releases cost, and in which years. Marvell disclosed the cancellation and the $711.8m of charges but never sized the cancelled programmes or named the affected product lines.
  • The maximum leverage ratio in the 2025 revolving credit facility. It is the sole maintenance covenant in the structure and its threshold is in a credit-agreement exhibit not held here.

Three limitations of what is currently observable also bear on the conclusions above. The holder base behind three say-on-pay revolts in seven years and a 36.9% independent-chairman vote is not established, so whether those votes reflect index-policy voting or a concentrated active holder is unknown, which matters because none of the three revolts changed a grant practice. Quarterly financial history is twelve quarters deep, so the FY2023-to-FY2025 communications collapse from $3,511m to $1,603m appears only as annual points, and the quarterly shape of that decline — how long distributor sell-in held reported revenue above sell-through, and what inventory days did at the peak — is the closest in-house analogue for an AI digestion quarter at a company recognizing 43% of revenue on sell-in. And the era before FY2017 is not quantified: the FY2015-to-FY2017 decline from $3,637m to $2,301m and the Audit Committee investigation into revenue pull-ins that removed both founders are the only completed peak-to-trough and the sole channel-accounting precedent this company has, and they precede the archived filings.

Finally, the Investor Day on 2026-10-06 falls five weeks after the 2026-08-28 data cut and management has said it will reset the long-term operating model there. The custom-versus-merchant margin split, the custom revenue base, the market-size estimate and the Google warrant expectation are the four figures most likely to move, and each is caveated above.

Appendix A — Investor-presentation insights and key slides

Fifteen decks from 2017 to 2026 with 945 rendered slides contain material Marvell has never put in a filing. The insights below are woven into the body sections named after each; this is the consolidated view.

  • Custom programme economics exist only in a deck. Each custom accelerator is multi-billion-dollar lifetime revenue over an 18-to-24-month window and each attach programme several hundred million over two to four years, against a pipeline of more than 50 opportunities across more than 10 customers worth $75bn of lifetime revenue, one third accelerator and two thirds attach by count [deck: Custom AI Investor Event 2025-06-17, slide 23]. The 18-to-24-month life is the most consequential number in the deck set and is the basis of the durability assessment in §3.1 and the socket arithmetic in §1.1.
  • The socket table, split by customer tier. Eighteen custom compute sockets at June 2025: twelve at the top four US hyperscalers (three accelerator plus nine attach) and six at emerging hyperscalers [deck: 2025-06-17, slides 22 and 113]. Two thirds of the won sockets are at four buyers, which the 10-K's concentration disclosure cannot show because it reports by revenue and not by programme (§4.1).
  • The market restatement, in two visible steps. The CY2028 data-center market went from $75bn to $94bn in fourteen months on an unchanged CY2023 base and an unchanged source list, with compute up 29% and interconnect up 37% [deck: 2025-06-17, slide 16, against 2024-04-11, slide 34]. Inside the April 2024 deck itself, two consecutive slides move CY2028 custom compute from $27.5bn to $42.9bn purely by raising custom's assumed share of accelerated compute from 16% to 25% [slides 29 and 30]. That assumption is unchanged in the 2025 deck; the growth since came from the base (§8).
  • The only quantified IP claims Marvell publishes. Custom dense SRAM at 17x the bandwidth per unit area of the best available third-party 1Mb instance with 50% lower area at equal bandwidth and 66% lower standby power; custom HBM base dies releasing 1.7x useful compute area and cutting memory I/O power 75%; package-integrated voltage regulation cutting total product power 15%; die-to-die interconnect at 10–20 Tbps/mm today with a roadmap above 50 Tbps/mm; packaging density from 1x at 2D to 16x at 4.5D [deck: 2025-06-17, slides 91, 95, 97, 98, 108]. None appears in any filing (§2).
  • Management's own margin warning, four years early. The 2021 investor day includes a gross-margin-by-end-market chart placing data center below the corporate average, enterprise networking above it, carrier below and automotive/industrial at the top [deck: 2021-10-06, slide 120] — in the same deck that set the 64–66% gross-margin target. Data center went from 40% of revenue in Q2 FY2022 to 79% in Q2 FY2027 and non-GAAP gross margin from 64.8% to 58.9%, roughly 100 basis points per ten points of mix (§13.4).
  • The target-model history, and its disappearance. Four published long-term models — 2017, 2018, 2020 and 2021 — then none. The AI Day 2024, the June 2025 custom event and the March 2026 corporate overview publish no financial model at all [decks: 2017-03-10 slide 90; 2018-10-16 slide 109; 2020-10-08 slide 112; 2021-10-06 slide 122]. Gross margin missed the last published target by 450 to 650 basis points while operating margin came within about 270, and the difference is the operating-expense line, which declined from 34.1% of revenue in Q2 FY2022 to 22.3% in Q2 FY2027 (§14).
  • Four commercial models the filings do not name. Buy (standard product), partner (custom on a Marvell design using customer IP), build (custom on a customer design using Marvell IP) and integrate (a build-to-spec chiplet combined with customer, partner and memory chiplets) [deck: Corporate Overview 2026-03-05, slide 15]. This taxonomy shows where the custom-versus-merchant boundary falls, and it explains why a single "custom" revenue figure spans several different economics (§1.1).
  • The four-tier distance map of the portfolio. Scale across (hundreds of kilometres: DCI modules, coherent and coherent-lite DSPs, TIAs, drivers, switches), scale out (about one kilometre: PAM DSPs, coherent-lite, analog, switches), scale up (metres: AEC DSPs, linear equalizers, analog, PCIe and Ethernet retimers, Ethernet/ESUN/UALink/PCIe switches, CXL expanders, co-packaged optics) and scale in (millimetres: die-to-die I/O and SerDes) [deck: Q2 FY2027 results 2026-08-27, slide 6]. The scale-up tier is where Celestial AI, XConn, UALink and ESUN land, and it is where nothing has shipped (§2).
  • The interconnect scaling arithmetic behind the demand case. 128 accelerators need 128 optical interconnects; 1,000 need 2,000; 25,000 need 75,000; 100,000 need 500,000; 1 million need 10 million; and interconnect speed doubles every two years in the AI era against every four years before it [deck: AI Day 2024-04-11, slides 38–39]. This is the mechanism behind the optical-port driver in §1.2 and §6.
  • The FY2025 data-center composition, disclosed once. $4.2bn split into approximately $3.7bn of cloud AI and approximately $0.5bn of on-premise, with custom above 25% of data-center revenue in Q4 FY2025 and targeted above 50% over time [deck: 2025-06-17, slide 29]. Applying that share to FY2026 data-center revenue reproduces management's ~$1.5bn custom figure (§1.1).
  • Four "next $1 billion" franchises promoted and then exited. Automotive Ethernet held a full investor-day section with design wins at 28 OEMs, content of $5.00–$8.50 per high-volume car, a 39% port CAGR and a share target raised from a third to more than half [decks: 2020-10-08 slide 88; 2021-10-06 slides 83–87], and was sold in 2025. Arm server processors added a stated $4bn of addressable market [deck: 2018-10-16 slides 61, 65–66], and were discontinued. 5G RAN was framed as the "industry's only provider of optimized 5G RAN silicon" with 4x the content of a 4G base station [decks: 2018-10-16 slides 80–81; 2021-10-06 slides 96, 100], and is now part of the communications line. Wi-Fi was one of three pillars in 2017 and was divested. The pattern bears on the durability of the custom claim (§9, §11).
  • The addressable-market ratchet across nine years. $8bn core markets (2017), $16bn on the Cavium announcement, $18bn (2018), $16bn→$20bn (2020), $17bn→$23bn on the Inphi announcement, $20bn→$30bn (2021), then a change of unit of account to data-center-only: $21bn→$75bn (2024) and $21bn→$94bn (2025) [decks: 2017-03-10 slide 29 through 2025-06-17 slide 17]. Every acquisition announcement raised the stated market (§11).
  • Process lead time, which is the switching-cost argument. Three to four years elapse from a foundry process being enabled, through test-chip IP validation, to a product shipping, across N5P, N3P, N2P, A16 and A14 [deck: 2025-06-17, slide 76]. This is the mechanism behind first-to-market cadence in §2 and §3.2, and it is also why a lost generation cannot be recovered inside one cycle.
  • Deal-level synergy framing, stated once and never reported against. Cavium at $150–175m of run-rate cost synergies within eighteen months, later raised to $200m ($50m in cost of goods sold, $150m in operating expenses), against combined last-quarter-annualized revenue of $3,427m; Inphi at $125m within eighteen months against $3,632m, financed with $4,000m of new debt at about 3.0x gross leverage on closing [decks: 2017-11-20 slides 10–11; 2018-10-16 slides 106–107; 2020-10-29 slides 16–18] (§11).
  • Customer count against socket concentration. Customers above $100m of revenue went from 8 (2018) to 13, 17 and 19 (2021), with Inphi adding four more at close [decks: 2018-10-16 slide 92; 2021-10-06 slide 23; 2020-10-29 slides 4 and 17]. Against that broadening count, the custom socket base concentrates at four buyers, and reported revenue concentration rose every year (§4.1).

Appendix C — External data sources

One external dataset is registered for a semiconductor company of this type. It has not been pulled.

DRAM and NAND spot pricing (memory_spot_pricing). A price series for dynamic random-access memory and NAND flash, covering spot quotations and contract-price direction. It measures what the memory layer of the supply chain charges, and at what direction of travel, on an irregular cadence. The comprehensive series is a paid subscription and there is no coded connector, so any collection would be a partial mosaic assembled from scattered cited price points.

It would inform two sections. In §6 it would test the memory-scarcity driver directly: management named DRAM scarcity as the reason customers are "modifying and adjusting their plans to actually use more of this type of technology", pulling demand into CXL memory expanders and near-memory compute, and that driver reverses when memory supply normalizes, so a price series is the leading indicator for whether the CXL attach franchise is a structural content gain or a scarcity substitution. In §13's operational-KPI subsection it would run against the storage and on-premise line and against the custom bill-of-materials pass-through discussed in §5, where Micron's 84.6% gross margin in the quarter ended 2026-05-28 is the clearest measure of where the memory layer's pricing power currently is. Marvell states that the largest hyperscalers buy their own high-bandwidth memory, so the exposure is in the emerging-hyperscaler turnkey programmes.

The series has not been pulled, and any collection would be a partial mosaic.
